transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos, Priya Patel (Redwood) / Alex Rivera, Samira Khan, Jon Park, Evan Li (Constellation)
Shared links: partner checklist: https://redwood.example.com/constellation/marketplace-checklist, ref-arch draft: /drive/Con-Redwood-RefArch-v1.pdf

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Diego and Priya on the call, super excited to sync on the marketplace integration.
[00:12] Alex Rivera: Thanks Maya, we appreciate it, we've been looking forward, Alex here. Quick note, we have Jon and Samira from product and Evan from security on to cover the compliance bits.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Awesome, do you want a quick agenda? We'll go over listing requirements, the reference arch, packaging options (AMI vs container), some perf/bench expectations, and then security checklist.
[00:33] Jon Park: Sounds good. We want to understand what artifacts you need from us and how the listing process timeline looks.
[00:40] Diego Ramos: Great — from a tech side I'll run through the ref-arch. A slight heads up, some of my notes reference Redwood Dedicate and Redwood Private but that might get transcribed wrong later.
[00:50] Samira Khan: Haha, yep, and we might call it Red Wood in our docs, so no worries.

[02:05] Diego Ramos: Alright, so high-level reference architecture: we recommend a marketplace image approach for Constellation where you can offer a pre-baked VM/AMI that includes our inference runtime plus an operator for autoscaling. The flow is: customer spins marketplace instance in their VPC, bootstrap script pulls model artifacts from Redwood model store (or you can host S3), registers with the Constellation control plane, and then the instance joins the dedicated pool.
[02:32] Jon Park: Quick clarifying q — you said the runtime pulls model artifacts, do we need to provide model binaries or can Redwood host them?
[02:38] Diego Ramos: Both are supported. For initial launch we suggest Redwood-hosted artifacts to make the listing lighter — we provide a signed manifest + URL. For enterprise customers they can bring their own model bundle.

[04:01] Priya Patel: I'll add that we also support a containerized package that runs in Constellation's managed k8s marketplace. The tradeoff: AMI/VM has lower ops for some customers and simpler image-based billing, whereas container gives you easier upgrades and smaller images.
[04:21] Alex Rivera: Noted. For Constellation's billing marketplace we prefer images but we can also support a container offering as an alternative SKU.

[05:10] Evan Li: From security, we need details on SSO/SAML integration and KMS key handling. Will the image require a customer-managed KMS or do you support Redwood-managed keys?
[05:20] Diego Ramos: Good q. We support both modes. For the marketplace we can default to Redwood-managed keys for the demo listing, but for production enterprise listings we require customer-managed KMS/HSM — and we have docs on integrating with AWS KMS and external HSMs. We'll send the specific KMS flow.
[05:41] Evan Li: Also audit logs — we need to confirm retention and what events are exported.
[05:47] Priya Patel: We can export audit events to a customer's CloudWatch or Stackdriver equivalent; retention is configurable but for the marketplace listing we'd document the default 30-day retention and how to extend it.

[07:00] Jon Park: On licensing and support — do you have a reference SLA for marketplace customers?
[07:08] Maya Chen: Yes, we offer a base support tier for the marketplace listing, and then enterprise customers can buy Redwood Dedicated support with an SLA. We'll share the support matrix in the partner packet.

[08:15] Diego Ramos: Back to the ref-arch doc, we have two recommended deployment profiles: 'small' for dev/testing (1 GPU vCPU mix, low mem), and 'production' profiles with autoscaling groups, warm KV cache, and quantization enabled to reduce memory footprint. Note: in our notes I wrote KV cash sometimes, so apologies if the transcript says cash.
[08:41] Samira Khan: Ha, good to know. For production we need a sample cost estimate and perf numbers to show customers.
[08:49] Diego Ramos: We can provide benchmark numbers for a 8k sequence workload on T4 and A100 equivalents — I'll attach the spreadsheet. It will include latency and tokens/sec.

[10:05] Alex Rivera: Can you also include a suggested pricing SKU we can surface in the marketplace UI?
[10:11] Maya Chen: We typically give recommended list price ranges, but Constellation can set final pricing. We'll share a pricing guidance doc based on model family and profile.

[12:00] Jon Park: About the listing assets — what do you need from us? Screenshots, logos, a description, and any security attestations?
[12:09] Maya Chen: Exactly. The partner checklist we shared lists: product images (1024x512), logo svg, short description (150 chars), long description, a 2-minute demo video link, support contact, and a security attestation form. Link is in the chat.

[13:22] Diego Ramos: For the technical package we'll provide: ref-arch diagram, bootstrap script, systemd unit example, a healthcheck endpoint, and a small smoke test that validates the model endpoint on first boot.
[13:35] Evan Li: Healthcheck and auth are key. What auth modes do you support — token-based, mTLS?
[13:41] Priya Patel: We support token-based API keys, short-lived tokens via our control plane, and mTLS for private deployments. On marketplace AMIs we recommend token + optional customer-managed mTLS for higher security.

[15:00] Alex Rivera: Regarding the joint solution — Constellation wants to market a co-branded listing and maybe run a webinar. Timeline thoughts?
[15:07] Maya Chen: We proposed a soft launch in late April and a public co-marketing push in early May. That lines up with our QA tests and security review.
[15:20] Jon Park: We need the final assets by Apr 18 to hit May PR.
[15:25] Maya Chen: Noted — that's in the action items.

[17:30] Evan Li: Back to security — SOC2 alignment, where are your audit logs stored, and can we get an attestation?
[17:38] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II in our control plane. For marketplace images, audit logs are forwarded to the customer's logging endpoint; we can provide an attestation doc and our SOC2 report under NDA.
[17:53] Evan Li: Great, we'll request the SOC2 under NDA. Also for data residency, some customers want EU-only hosting; how do you support region pinning?
[18:01] Diego Ramos: We support region pinning for both hosted and private deployments. For marketplace images, Constellation can restrict the AMI to EU regions or offer region-specific listings.

[20:00] Samira Khan: One operational question — upgrades. When you release a new model or runtime patch, how does the marketplace handle upgrade notifications?
[20:08] Priya Patel: The image-based flow will expose a metadata endpoint with version info; Constellation's marketplace can show an update available banner. For container-based listings we recommend using a rolling upgrade mechanism. We can also provide a webhook so you can notify subscribed customers when a critical patch is released.

[22:15] Jon Park: Any private deployment concerns? A number of our enterprise users ask for on-prem options.
[22:23] Diego Ramos: Yes we have Redwood Private which is customer-controlled; for that we provide a private control plane option and an air-gapped install. There are extra steps for key management and network peering. We'll add a note in the ref-arch doc for private installs.

[24:40] Alex Rivera: For our marketplace listing flow there is a vendor intake form that includes legal terms — is there anything special we should expect on Redwood's side for indemnity or data handling?
[24:50] Maya Chen: Standard vendor terms. For enterprise customers, we negotiate specific DPA/KDAs. For the marketplace listing, we typically accept the Constellation marketplace vendor terms and then enterprise customers sign mutual agreements. Legal can sync if needed.

[27:00] Diego Ramos: I'm going to walk through the ref-arch diagram quickly — slide share now. (Some brief screen sharing noises)
[27:08] Diego Ramos: Top left is the Constellation marketplace catalog, user clicks deploy, it spins an AMI into the customer's VPC, bootstrap script runs, it authenticates with Redwood control plane over TLS, downloads model manifest, warms KV cache, then opens port 443 with the model endpoint. Notes: set readiness probe to 200ms and liveness to 5s.
[27:34] Samira Khan: The warming KV cache — does that add startup latency?
[27:38] Diego Ramos: Yes it can add a minute for large models, hence we suggest a warm standby or pre-warmed snapshot for faster start. We'll include scripts to restore a pre-warm.

[29:50] Evan Li: For encryption in transit are we using TLS 1.3?
[29:54] Priya Patel: Yes TLS 1.3 by default, mutual TLS optional.

[31:10] Jon Park: Benchmarks — can you share the tests you ran and the raw data?
[31:17] Diego Ramos: Yes, spreadsheet will have raw outputs. We ran RPS and tail latency p95/p99 with varying token lengths. Caveat: results vary by infra — labeled as 'reference' not guaranteed.

[33:00] Maya Chen: Switching to go-to-market: co-branding, joint webinar, and possible case study down the line. We should decide a point person for marketing assets.
[33:12] Alex Rivera: I'll be the marketing lead from Constellation side.
[33:15] Maya Chen: Great — add Alex to the asset request thread, we'll loop in our content team.

[34:40] Samira Khan: Are there any known limitations with Redwood Dedicated when running in Constellation's env?
[34:48] Diego Ramos: No major limitations but a few notes: GPU driver compat can differ across marketplace images, we recommend standardizing kernel versions. Also if customers want autoscaling across regions, we need cross-region S3 or model replication.

[36:00] Evan Li: For audit events, can you map event names to our schema? We have a specific event taxonomy.
[36:07] Priya Patel: Yes we can map and provide a sample JSON log schema. We'll need Evan's event schema to align.

[38:20] Jon Park: Timeline recap — we need assets by Apr 18, security deep-dive scheduled Apr 14, ref-arch final by Apr 18. Public PR early May.
[38:30] Maya Chen: I'll send a calendar invite for Apr 14 security deep-dive with Evan. Diego will upload ref-arch by Apr 18.

[40:00] Alex Rivera: A couple quick questions on support routing: will Constellation customers open tickets to Constellation or Redwood?
[40:07] Maya Chen: For marketplace listings we'll support a tiled support model: basic support via Constellation with escalation to Redwood SEs for infra or runtime bugs. We'll document the triage flow.

[42:10] Diego Ramos: One small gotcha I want to call out — if your marketplace VM image gets customized by customers it can break our healthchecks; include a recommended whitelist of sysctl changes.
[42:22] Samira Khan: Good call, we'll add that to the vendor guidelines.

[44:00] Maya Chen: Any blockers on your side?
[44:05] Jon Park: No blockers, just need the artifacts and security answers.
[44:08] Evan Li: I'll put together the security questionnaire and send it back by Apr 14.

[46:30] Maya Chen: Ok final recap: action items in the chat, Diego and Maya to upload artifacts, Evan to run security Q, Alex to be marketing lead — we'll reconvene after the security deep-dive.
[46:45] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
[46:52] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and a calendar invite.

[51:30] call ended

Notes on transcript: Minor transcription errors expected (Redwood Dedicate / KV cash). Deck/asset links are references, actual files in partner drive.
notes: Shared deck link in chat; agreed to SOC2 under NDA and scheduled security deep-dive. Ref-arch will include AMI bootstrap script and healthchecks. Marketing lead: Alex Rivera.
